claims.text: Embedding hBN into a Ni-based matrix by powder metallurgy will produce a high-temperature self-lubricating composite.
The Ni-hBN composite will exhibit stable tribological performance from room temperature to at least 900 °C.
Powder-metallurgy co-processing followed by high-temperature sintering or hot pressing will consolidate the Ni-based alloy and hBN powders.
The proposed processing will produce uniformly distributed hBN lamellae within the Ni-based matrix.
hBN acts as a solid lubricant at elevated temperatures.
The Ni-based matrix maintains mechanical integrity at elevated temperatures.
The combined lubrication by hBN and mechanical integrity of the Ni-based matrix promote stable friction over a broad temperature range.
The composite's coefficient of friction will remain low and stable from room temperature to about 900 °C.
The composite's wear rate will remain low and stable from room temperature to about 900 °C.
The composite will not suffer a significant loss of matrix mechanical strength up to about 900 °C.
Oxidation may degrade the composite's performance above 900 °C.
Insufficient hBN dispersion may degrade the composite's performance.
Matrix microstructural changes may degrade the composite's performance above 900 °C.
